TypeScript vs JavaScript and type erasure

TypeScript adds a static type system to JavaScript and emits JavaScript; most type annotations have no
runtime representation.

A typed price function still needs validation when called from external JavaScript.

Read the diagram: Compilation checks declared types, but the output cannot enforce them by annotation alone.

Interview question: Does TypeScript make every runtime error impossible?
Answer: No. It catches many static errors but cannot guarantee runtime correctness.
